name: Black nationalism
summary: Black nationalism holds that people of African descent form a distinct nation with a right to self-determination, community control of their own politics and economy, and pride in Black history and culture. Strands range from Garvey's back-to-Africa program to Malcolm X's call for community control and self-defense and the Panthers' revolutionary socialist version; it rejects integration as dependence on white institutions and treats racial redress as owed.
scope: The mainstream twentieth-century American strand: Marcus Garvey and the UNIA's 1920 Declaration of Rights, Malcolm X's 1964 Ballot or the Bullet, and the 1966 Black Panther Ten-Point Program, as described in Wikipedia's overview. It excludes Black supremacist doctrine and religions such as the Nation of Islam's teachings on race. Economic, religious and gender answers vary by strand and most are inferred at low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Marcus Garvey
keyFigures.role: Founder of the UNIA, whose ideas became known as Garveyism.

keyFigures.name: Malcolm X
keyFigures.role: Leading nationalist voice of the 1960s, author of the Ballot or the Bullet speech.

keyFigures.name: Huey P. Newton
keyFigures.role: Co-founder of the Black Panther Party and author of its Ten-Point Program.

sources.usedFor: Garveyite claims on rights, self-defense, Africa, segregation, education and armed service.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Panther programs ran community clinics and the program demands decent basic needs, so guaranteed care is an inferred fit.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Panther program attacks economic exploitation of Black workers, so higher legal pay floors are inferred as supported.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Adherents split between Garvey-style Black capitalism and Marxist-Leninist Panthers, so no single answer holds.

public-ownership.rationale: The Panthers wanted means of production placed in community hands, but other strands favor private Black business, so the strands divide.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the Panthers' demand to end exploitation and Malcolm X's complaint about uncompensated Black labor.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the focus on Black workers' economic power and solidarity; the sources never discuss unions directly.

property-fundamental.rationale: Reparations in land and community takeover of idle production imply property can be overridden for justice; inferred only.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The Panther program says employers who fail to provide full employment should lose control of production, implying tighter control of firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: Panther survival programs and job or income guarantees imply support for public provision, so cutting welfare is opposed by inference.

worker-ownership.rationale: Community ownership of production is proposed by the Panthers, but worker-by-worker ownership is not addressed and other strands favor Black entrepreneurs.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Adherents distrust state security forces that target Black communities, so surveillance is opposed by inference.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Malcolm X lists drug addiction among evils the Black community must clean up itself, implying opposition to legal recreational use.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Declaration affirms free speech yet protests defamation of Black people, so adherents pull both ways.

strong-leader.rationale: Garvey's UNIA claimed a provisional leader of the Black race, but other strands favor community democracy; not clearly settled.

state-harmful.rationale: Adherents seek their own state or community power rather than no state, so the statement is rejected by inference.

limit-guns.rationale: The Panther program invokes the Second Amendment for armed self-defense and Malcolm X endorsed owning rifles and shotguns.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Panther program centers ending police brutality and murder of Black people, so more police power is firmly opposed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Malcolm X's social program targets vice in the community; inferred opposition.

decide-locally.rationale: Malcolm X defines freedom as communities controlling their own politics and economy, favoring local control.

rehabilitation.rationale: The Panther program calls for releasing Black prisoners denied fair trials, hinting at skepticism toward punitive prisons; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Cultural nationalists such as Karenga's US Organization assigned distinct family roles; strands differ and sources give little detail.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: No source states a position; inferred from the socially conservative cultural-nationalist strand, with the Panthers more mixed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not discussed in the sources and adherents are divided.

more-religion-public.rationale: Malcolm X wants all faiths united behind nationalism, but Marxist strands are secular; split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The Panther program demands reparations of land and money for slavery and exploitation, and Malcolm X insists on redress.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by sources; cultural nationalist doctrine assigns fixed roles, so inferred disagreement.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Pride in Black culture and achievement is described as a core belief, with Black history teaching demanded by the Panthers.

gradual-change.rationale: Malcolm X rejects patient appeals to white conscience and the Declaration justifies forceful resistance.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; the Declaration claims free movement while the focus is on Black self-determination.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The Declaration rejects the League of Nations for Black people, yet Malcolm X later appealed to the UN; no settled view.

free-trade.rationale: Self-reliance and anti-colonial thinkers like Fanon and Nkrumah lead to suspicion of free trade; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Statement refers to a country; adherents put the Black nation first but the sources do not say how it treats global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No source addresses it and anti-colonial strands distrust intervention while solidarity favors protection of Black peoples.

open-borders.rationale: The Declaration claims a right to travel within and between nations, supporting freer movement by inference.

limit-growth.rationale: Not a topic in the sources.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not a topic in the sources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not a topic in the sources.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not a topic in the sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Declaration justifies resisting oppression with force and the Panther program echoes the right to dissolve destructive governments.

experts-over-public.rationale: Malcolm X wants ordinary Black people to control their own communities rather than outside authorities; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Panther Marxism and Garvey capitalism pull apart.

socialized-markets.rationale: The Panther program puts production and housing in community cooperatives, which fits public or collective ownership alongside markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: No nationalist source discusses tax design; adherents hold no common view on a land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Sources never address inheritance tax; Panther redistribution points one way, Black-business strands the other.

basic-income.rationale: The Panther program demands that government guarantee every person a job or guaranteed income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Black economic self-sufficiency and community ownership imply support for protecting Black-owned enterprise; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Panthers wanted state aid for cooperatives but other strands rely on private enterprise.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Malcolm X urges Black people to own their stores and businesses, favoring spread of small ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Programs demand jobs and income, not abolition of wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are absent from the sources; the nearest concern is Black-owned banks, not abolishing central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not part of any strand's program; inferred disagreement.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Declaration demands the right to elect representatives and Malcolm X endorses the ballot.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Declaration invokes the Declaration of Independence and elected representation, not hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Malcolm X calls the ballot a weapon and the Declaration claims the right to elect representatives.

direct-votes.rationale: Malcolm X stresses the ballot but no source addresses referendums over representation, so no stance is inferable.

workers-councils.rationale: Panther community control resembles councils but no source states it.

right-to-secede.rationale: Separatist strands such as the Nation of Islam discussed a separate Black state in the South, supporting secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Declaration affirms equal legal rights for all, so natural rulers is rejected by inference.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Declaration asserts the right to resist oppression by force and the Panthers vowed to protect the community by whatever means necessary.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Declaration discourages Black men from serving imperial armies, implying no celebration of war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Malcolm X draws on religion and welcomes all faiths, while Marxist strands are secular.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Malcolm X stays out of religious disputes and seeks unity across faiths, so scripture-based law is inferred as disfavored.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Panthers demand juries of peers and public accountability, not private provision.

military-superiority.rationale: The Panthers and the Declaration oppose service in the national military, so superiority is not a goal.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Core belief treats people of African descent as a single nation with a claim to self-governance.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Revolutionary nationalists take Marxist views; cultural nationalists stress race instead.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Panther demands for jobs, housing and reparations reach beyond equal opportunity; inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Claim that African land belongs to Africans suggests sympathy for indigenous land claims; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Declaration lists colonization of Africa as a grievance and claims African land for Africans and the diaspora.

civilizational-union.rationale: The movement overlaps with Pan-Africanism and treats dispersed Africans as one people.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Adherents stress solidarity and collective self-reliance over individual selfishness.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Karenga's Kawaida stresses duties but others stress rights; unresolved.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is outside the movement's documented concerns, leaving no basis for a position.

limit-population.rationale: Not directly discussed; a movement seeking nation-building would be wary of limiting Black population growth.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from focus on economic empowerment within modern economies.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technology and institutional disruption do not feature in the sources; adherents have no shared line.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is not discussed in nationalist programs, so neutral by default rather than split on evidence.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Community control by people themselves is the emphasis; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Distrust of police and state surveillance implies support for private communication; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Adherents seek transformation of the present order of white control, not a restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Strands are strongly ideological in different ways, and the sources give no view on pragmatism versus ideology.

direct-action.rationale: Malcolm X pairs the ballot with the bullet and the Panthers used armed patrols, so adherents use both routes.

means-match-ends.rationale: Malcolm X's ballot-and-bullet pragmatism and the Panthers' armed patrols do not settle whether means must mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing in the movement supports it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Panther programs ask for jobs and production under community control, not abolition of specialization.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Panther demands include bread and housing but sources do not endorse need-based distribution generally.

production-for-use.rationale: Marxist strands favor it; capitalist nationalists do not.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Panther program demands an end to capitalist exploitation of the Black community and Malcolm X condemns unpaid Black labor.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Panthers were Marxist-Leninist but their program stresses community control by Black people, not class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Panther demands include cooperative housing and land, but collective farming is not discussed.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Revolutionary strands drew on Mao and Fanon but others do not hold this.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Declaration objects to taxation without representation, not taxation itself.

harm-principle.rationale: Sources do not address limits on state power over adults in general, and strands differ on moral policing.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Core belief is a collective claim to nationhood and self-governance by Black people.

conscription.rationale: The Panther program demands exemption of Black men from military service and the Declaration discourages serving imperial armies.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Emigration advocates and nation-within-a-nation advocates differ.

state-as-business.rationale: Panthers want state accountable to community needs, not run as business.

positive-liberty.rationale: Malcolm X ties freedom to political, economic and social control of the community.

media-academia-power.rationale: Black nationalists criticize mainstream education and media for Black history omissions, but no source ranks their power against elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Movement counters internalized racism and treats critics' pseudo-science claims as rejected; inferred.

total-state.rationale: Self-reliance and community control oppose a state directing all of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Ethiopianism and Garveyism speak of Africa's coming greatness and racial uplift.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Claims are for return of African land and self-determination, not expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Declaration appeals to elected representation and equal law.

bound-labor.rationale: Movement grew from resistance to slavery and peonage-like labor, so bound labor is firmly rejected.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Panther demand for education in the true history of Black people presumes mainstream teaching reflects who holds power.

universal-morality.rationale: Nothing in the sources commits adherents on universal reason-based morality; religious and secular strands differ.

single-common-good.rationale: Sources describe interest-based Black community politics but do not address whether politics has one rationally found common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Garveyism was partly inspired by Zionism, but some nationalists have been hostile; adherents split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The Declaration says the African diaspora has a stake in Africa and claims African land for Africans at home and abroad.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not part of the documented program, though Swahili was adopted in some cultural nationalist circles; no stance is inferable from sources read.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Community control of means of production implies democratic say in running firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Community control of schools is favored but vouchers are not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not discussed; Panther job guarantees point toward spending while Black capitalists differ.

economic-freedom.rationale: Malcolm X wants Black ownership of business but does not frame freedom this way.

rule-by-example.rationale: Declaration relies on laws and legal rights.

national-self-determination.rationale: The first Panther point demands power to determine the destiny of the Black community and the movement seeks representation as a nation.

force-without-un.rationale: Not discussed; mixed distrust of both great powers and the UN.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Religion plays a central role for Malcolm X and the Nation of Islam.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The Declaration extends rights beyond nation-state borders.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Panther programs demand guaranteed income and survival programs without work tests.

class-collaboration.rationale: Panther class struggle stands against capitalist Black nationalists; adherents split.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Panthers demand education in Black heritage; not destroying culture.

dominated-front.rationale: Revolutionary nationalists drew on Fanon, Mao and Nkrumah and Pan-African groups link worldwide.

workers-nation.rationale: Revolutionary strands drew on international class thinking while cultural nationalists organize by race; no common answer.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Karenga's US Organization assigned distinct roles while Black feminists and many Panthers challenged them.

ban-interest.rationale: Malcolm X wants Black banks, implying lending is acceptable.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Declaration protests separate and inferior facilities and Malcolm X defines segregation as outside control, not voluntary separation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Panther Marxism and Malcolm X's complaint of outside control describe the state as a tool of the dominant.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is absent from the documented positions.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Movement rejects integration and assimilation as a goal for Black people.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory of the white right that adherents would reject.

proportional-representation.rationale: Early proponents sought democratic representation in plural societies, which minority representation fits.

national-mission.rationale: Adherents want self-determination, not spreading a government to others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Black feminists said movements were sexist while some nationalists stress race first.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Malcolm X calls America's conscience bankrupt and attacks political delay of civil rights by the major parties.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is inconsistent with the movement's stress on dignity.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Panther program demands an end to police murder and brutality.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Panther demands for jobs, housing and education require an active state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Separatist strands historically preferred racial separation; the sources do not state this directly.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration asserts equal rights before the law for all and Black people's right to life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Doctrine on socialist stages abroad is not in the sources; only the Marxist-Leninist strand would care.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Malcolm X says he does not consider himself an American and sees things as the victim; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law is not discussed in the sources; nationalists stress equal rights but also group autonomy.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not discussed; no tradition supports it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Malcolm X welcomes all faiths in the movement but no source addresses religious instruction in state schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine on the socialist state is outside the sources' coverage of this movement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Panther program echoes the Declaration of Independence's right to dissolve destructive government and the UNIA Declaration protests taxation without representation.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are not discussed; self-reliance suggests nothing definite about export balances.

population-transfer.rationale: Adherents sought voluntary emigration, not coerced removal of minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Panthers framed force as defensive but accepted resistance by any means.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Black organisations have been targeted by state bans and repression.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Malcolm X says a community is segregated when outsiders control it, which echoes domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Declaration and Panther texts invoke founding rights but do not discuss the structure of divided government.

vanguard-party.rationale: Panthers followed Leninist ideas while cultural nationalists did not.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Panther program prioritises housing, bread and jobs for poor Black communities.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Panthers favored housing cooperatives but not individual purchase.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Panthers blame exploitation and institutions for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Separatists see value in separation but others seek multi-racial coalitions.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection by lot is not found in any nationalist source; elections are assumed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Panther program demands fair trial and juries of peers because Black people have suffered from legal abuses.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Panther food programs and demand for bread suggest support.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Declaration affirms freedom of speech.

party-commands-army.rationale: Panthers had a Marxist-Leninist party structure but the sources do not speak to party command of armed forces; mild disagreement inferred from distrust of military power.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The Declaration claims free movement and rights for all.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Panthers were organized hierarchically while other strands were loose, and the sources give no common rule.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Pan-African unity favors union but sovereignty emphasis opposes it.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on elected, accountable representation.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church government is not addressed; Black churches are independent and congregational, but this is outside the sources read.

clerical-rule.rationale: Malcolm X sought unity across religions, so clerical rule is inferred as disfavored.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Declaration discourages Black men from serving imperial armies, which suggests refusing to back such wars.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Declaration affirms freedom of speech.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources.

recall-officials.rationale: Malcolm X wants the community to control politicians, which suggests accountability.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Panthers opposed military service and the Declaration discourages imperial armies.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Panthers proposed cooperative housing, not mandatory ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Panthers urged armed community self-defense under the Second Amendment.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The urban Black communities central to Malcolm X and the Panthers are not contrasted with rural life in the sources.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-African solidarity favors unity across borders drawn by colonizers.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Nationalists criticize white academia and Black moderates but also build educational institutions, so no clear stance.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Pride in Black culture to counter inequality implies equal worth of cultures, though some strands claimed Black superiority.

death-penalty.rationale: Panther demand for release of unfairly tried prisoners suggests distrust of capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sources are silent; cultural nationalists and Panthers likely differ on school sex education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Panthers wanted real history and knowledge in education.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Malcolm X names moral decay among evils to confront.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Diaspora claims on Africa suggest descent but sources do not state it.

minority-language-support.rationale: Panther demand for education about Black people suggests support for cultural education.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Sources do not address exemptions from general law; Malcolm X's concern is racial, not religious, discrimination.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Cultural nationalism stresses unity and shared standards.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Malcolm X says political freedom without economic control is empty and Panthers demand community ownership.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Panther preamble speaks of dissolving government but no source calls for an elected constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Declaration affirms freedoms of speech, religion and commerce.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear policy is absent from the sources.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Method of choosing a head of state is not discussed.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Malcolm X wants communities in control of their economy, so independent central banks are inferred as disliked.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions are not discussed in the sources; the nearest claim is to African land.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Panther demand to place idle production and housing in community hands implies property serves the community.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Debates over the Soviet Union's character are outside the sources about this movement.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not a topic in any source read.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance commitments are not discussed; nationalists distrust state military alliances, but no source states this.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Anti-colonial grievances over African land suggest this view.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Religion is a community institution for Malcolm X.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ceremonial head of state design is not discussed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Separatists claim the right to a separate territory.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One-country-two-systems arrangements are not covered by the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inconsistent with stress on equal rights.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Panther economic demands suggest progressive redistribution.

character-from-environment.rationale: Malcolm X blames social degradation and oppression for conditions in the community.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Declaration demands equal legal rights and fair trials.

space-expansion.rationale: Not discussed; priority is earthly community uplift.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional design is not discussed by any strand in the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: UNIA treated Garvey as a recognised leader but other strands do not.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is outside the sources, and gender-role strands differ.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Only the Marxist-Leninist Panther strand could take a view and the sources do not state one.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Panther program demands land as reparation and the Black nationalist heritage includes demand for land.

refugee-return.rationale: Return claims of the diaspora to Africa suggest sympathy.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Garveyite claims rest on African land for Africans and the diaspora, but whether a state may claim territory because co-nationals live there is not addressed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Malcolm X says religion should not divide.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress laws are not addressed in the sources; Nation of Islam dress norms are religious practice rather than a demand for law.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Declaration claims a single Black nation and Pan-Africanism treats Africans worldwide as one people.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The later nation-within-a-nation approach seeks self-governing institutions within the existing state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The movement is divided between emigration to Africa and the nation-within-a-nation approach.

ban-cartels.rationale: Panther opposition to economic concentration suggests support.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed; Panther anti-capitalism and Black-business strands diverge.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: As a minority, adherents rely on courts and amendments; majority-rule override is feared.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not discussed and strands differ on gender.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreement design is outside the sources.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Self-reliance targets the Black community, not a closed colonial bloc.

moral-incentives.rationale: Malcolm X urges community discipline, but no source discusses replacing material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Panther armed patrols but not clear adoption of foco theory.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The Panther program demands education in the true history of Black people and the Declaration says Black children should learn Black history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Declaration lists colonization of Africa among grievances.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Declaration adopts a flag and anthem for the Black race, implying loyalty teaching for the Black nation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The Panther program demands reparations, so racial remedies are favored.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Panther Marxism holds crisis claims while Black capitalists do not; the sources give no common answer.

delink-world-market.rationale: Garvey's trade ambitions and Panther anti-imperialism pull in opposite directions on integration into the world market.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: No source discusses theories of rich-country worker complicity; Fanon-influenced strands might, but it is not stated.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Declaration protests discrimination in jobs and public facilities.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Panthers cite the Second and Fourteenth Amendments and Declaration invokes the founding rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-colonial grievances over partition of Africa suggest support.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Declaration claims the right to elect representatives.

minority-veto.rationale: Not discussed; the nationalists want majority control of their own community.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Panther preamble asserts the right to abolish destructive government and the Declaration justifies resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary versus monarchical authority is not a nationalist concern in the sources.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics are absent from the movement's documented positions.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Nationalism stresses self-reliance more than elite duty, but no source states a view on the duty of the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Malcolm X urges using political power.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Malcolm X attacked pacifying appeals and Black moderates; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Malcolm X says America looks through victim eyes and appeals to white conscience fail; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Revolutionary nationalists drew on Fanon and Nkrumah's analyses of colonial extraction.

native-born-offices.rationale: Diaspora claims on African citizenship contradict it.

party-own-road.rationale: Revolutionary nationalists built independent movements drawing on varied thinkers.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Self-reliance and self-sufficiency are core stressed beliefs.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's land claims concern Africa and the American South, not recovery of lost war territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Delany's Africa for Africans slogan implies African leadership of Africa.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional anti-fascism is a European debate not covered in the sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Comparison of fascism and communism is not discussed; the Marxist-Leninist strand would object.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Malcolm X describes unrequited Black labor as history; the claim is denial of slavery's role.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from stress on Black history and dignity.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources focus on race, and Black feminist critique makes gender questions contested.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not addressed in the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Afrocentric and nationalist strands seek institutions of their own.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Panthers oppose military and police power.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care work is not discussed; Karenga's roles and Black feminist critiques point opposite ways.

filial-duty.rationale: Cultural nationalists stress family and community duty.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service recruitment is not discussed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Community ownership of its economy implies opposition to outside takeover.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not discussed, and family-values and Panther strands may differ.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Community control of politicians implies accountability.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Panthers cooperative land but not use-based tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Declaration protests taxation without representation.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land ownership by foreigners is not addressed, though Black community land ownership is valued.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Panthers attribute inequality to systemic injustice not just intent.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Malcolm X urges self-discipline and community building over status seeking.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Support for foreign insurgents is not discussed in the sources, though revolutionary strands admired anti-colonial fighters.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anti-colonial rejection of imposing control on others.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding of NGOs is not discussed.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy incentives are not discussed in the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local community control of economy and land supports limits on outside purchase.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Panther program says government should guarantee each person a job or income.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic peace theory is not discussed by the movement's sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Malcolm X says the government is unwilling to protect Black people, weakening duty to obey.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-colonial thought opposes domination of others but the sources do not state an absolute non-intervention principle.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in any source read.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Some nationalists promoted antisemitism, but typical adherents disclaim it.

informal-organisation.rationale: Panthers and UNIA built formal organisations.

local-production.rationale: Black-owned stores and businesses serving the community.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Declaration appeals to international rights over national law.

religious-nation.rationale: Malcolm X welcomes all faiths into the movement.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Opposed to subordination of Black peoples.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Community control of economy but not addressed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Panthers wanted production in community hands but no source speaks of personal belongings.

defeat-communism.rationale: Revolutionary strands are Marxist and others not anticommunist campaigners.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Sources do not address how public services should be delivered.

religion-illusion.rationale: Malcolm X and Nation of Islam hold religion central.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Black feminists said so; nationalists often did not.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of housework and childcare is not discussed, and strands differ on gender roles.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not a documented concern.

treaties-binding.rationale: Panthers invoked legal commitments such as reparations; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The Panther program proposes housing and land cooperatives.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settlement policy for minority-majority regions is not addressed; adherents would likely oppose coercive settlement but this is inferred only.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Panthers were Marxist-Leninist while Black-capitalist strands rejected communism, so a third-way claim is not shared.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Declaration claims African land for Africans.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a position of the movement.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from civil-rights and freedom emphasis.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Declaration affirms freedoms of speech and rights.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Malcolm X says not to argue over religious differences.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Declaration lists colonization of Africa among its grievances.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Malcolm X wants community members to control their politics.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Black feminists argued so while many nationalists stressed race.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical end-of-life policy is not discussed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Strands are explicitly left (Panthers) or centrist-capitalist (Garvey) and the sources contain no claim about the left-right divide.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Malcolm X and the Nation of Islam are Muslim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Garvey's movement was Christian and Malcolm X spoke as a Muslim, but the Panthers were secular; adherents are split.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on community self-expression and control against imposed norms; the sources do not discuss it.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from the Panther program's demand for justice and protection for vulnerable people; the sources do not discuss contracts.

social-market-economy.rationale: Strands run from Garveyite black capitalism to Panther socialism, so there is no common line.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The sources endorse armed self-defense, which implies not disarming, though they criticize use of the military against Black people; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the Panther demands for full employment and reparations and the call for community-wide economic uplift.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Garvey and Malcolm X looked to Africa and non-white solidarity rather than Western alliances; inferred and not directly stated.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from the movement's republican and community-control politics, though Garvey's UNIA used titled offices; not addressed in the sources.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Economic self-reliance and Black-owned institutions are core, so community-owned credit fits; not stated directly.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperial and self-determination stress of Garvey and the Panthers; the sources do not name lenders.

property-franchise.rationale: Malcolm X's Ballot or the Bullet and the UNIA Declaration demand full voting rights for Black people.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; strands differ on gender and ecology.

reification.rationale: The Panthers' Marxist strand might agree while Garveyites would not; the sources do not use the term.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Malcolm X and the Panthers condemned control of media and resources by white elites; the specific claim is inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Panther programme demands trial by a jury of peers and an end to arbitrary police power.

racial-franchise.rationale: Adherents want a Black self-governing community or state yet claim equal votes in America, so they are split on exclusive franchise.

online-participation.rationale: The sources predate the internet and say nothing on it.

open-government-data.rationale: The Panthers' demand for accountable policing and community control suggests transparency; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred; scope excludes the Nation of Islam's religious doctrine and the sources do not address marriage law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Black nationalists urged buying from Black-owned shops, but a boycott aimed at a religious minority is not in the sources.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Community control of institutions is central, which suits community deliberation; assemblies by lot are not mentioned.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Strands span Christian, Muslim and secular positions; the sources show no common view.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Panther program demands an end to the robbery of the Black community by capitalists, which treats concentrated wealth as a source of domination.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Strands differ on this and the sources do not address it; Garveyite and religious strands were conservative while Panther leaders later backed gay liberation.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Malcolm X and the Black church tradition treat religion as central to the community, so state-imposed atheism is inferred as rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Panther program demands an end to police brutality and community control of police, not abolition of policing.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The strand seeks self-determination or separation rather than power-sharing within one state, and the sources do not address consociational rule; inferred as split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Panther program demands that government and society provide jobs, housing and reparations, so reliance on charity is inferred as rejected.

term-limits.rationale: The sources never address term limits and adherents are not known to be split along any principle; inferred as neutral.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed in the sources; inferred as neutral.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the strand's priorities are immediate community survival and self-determination, so no clear stance is inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Adherents split: church-based and Garveyite strands kept male clerical leadership while Panther and later strands stressed women's equality.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Adherents split between patriarchal Garveyite and religious strands and the Panthers' later gender-equality commitments.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the Panther program's demand for decent housing for Black communities; rent caps are not mentioned.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Garvey's UNIA had uniformed bodies but the sources do not present youth drilling as a general position.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the Panther program's opposition to military service in wars of white power; nuclear basing is not discussed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperial stance of Black Power and the Panthers; the sources do not discuss bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The Panther program and nationalist demands for reparations treat past crimes against Black people as wrongs to be officially acknowledged.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Panther demand for full employment and economic justice.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Malcolm X, the Panther program and the Garveyite declaration endorse self-defence, including armed.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Black nationalism stresses a shared African heritage and history; the sources emphasise Black history and pride.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The sources note gender debates within the movement but give no common answer.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from reverence for Garvey, Malcolm X and fallen Panthers; the sources do not discuss sainthood.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Strands differ, and the scope excludes religions such as the Nation of Islam; not addressed.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Garvey's program gathers the diaspora in Africa while cultural nationalists accept diaspora; adherents are split.

culture-before-state.rationale: Strands differ between cultural nationalists and political separatists.

god-not-male.rationale: Strands differ on religion and the sources do not address this.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Strands differ on religion and gender and the sources do not address this.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Black nationalism demands community control of its own economy and opposes dependence on white-owned institutions.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Separatist strands and the Panther plebiscite demand a Black territory, while cultural strands do not; split.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred: the Panther program stresses community self-organisation and workers' needs; unions' independence is not addressed.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Panthers' revolutionary socialist version points this way, but Garvey's capitalist-leaning strand does not, so mild support.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the demand for community control of institutions and community clinics in the Panther program.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no shared position.

municipal-property.rationale: Malcolm X and the Panthers called for community control of the economy of Black neighbourhoods; ownership forms vary by strand.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; community control is favoured but confederations are not discussed.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the Panther program's demands for full employment and decent livelihoods; family wage is not addressed.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no shared position.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no shared position.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic: not addressed in the sources; strands differ on state versus community independence.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic: not addressed in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred: Black nationalism's claim of dignity and self-determination for persons denied it; not stated in these terms.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Garvey's UNIA and the Nation of Islam strand were religious, but the Panther strand was secular, so mild support.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed; community control is favoured but the national legislature's role is not discussed.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic: not addressed in the sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic: not addressed in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The overview and Garvey's Declaration treat people of African descent as a nation with distinct interests that should be organised and defended.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Black history, culture and heritage is a defining theme in the overview and the Declaration of Rights.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Malcolm X and the Panthers stressed armed self-defence and opposed imperial wars such as Vietnam, but the exact statement is not addressed.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Black nationalism defines the nation by shared descent, history and experience of oppression rather than language, so this is inferred from how the sources define the nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Malcolm X urged Black voting power and community control within the existing political system, and the sources show no demand for separate religious electorates; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Panther program condemns state police violence against Black communities but the sources do not frame it as a foreign plot against the country; inferred as split.

free-public-college.rationale: The Panther program demands education that teaches Black people their true history and equal provision of basic needs, so free public higher education is an inferred fit.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The sources never address environmental taxation, and strands from Garvey's capitalism to the Panthers' socialism would differ.

future-generations.rationale: Concern for Black children's future runs through the Garvey and Malcolm X programs, so a duty to those who come after is inferred, not stated on the environment.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Strands differ on gender, with male-led organizations often restricting women's roles while Panther women held leadership posts, so no single answer holds.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Panther program opposes Black men serving in the military, but the sources do not address national arms levels and the movement endorses armed self-defense.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Malcolm X wanted to bring the Black struggle before the United Nations, but the sources do not address secrecy in treaties; inferred as neutral.

capital-controls.rationale: The sources never address capital flows, and Garvey-style Black capitalism and Panther socialism would answer differently.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Malcolm X and the Panther program defend armed community self-defense against police and white violence, so an adherent rejects a state-only monopoly on arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Panther program demands exemption of Black men from military service in a racist government's wars, and Malcolm X opposed fighting for white America, though Garvey's UNIA supported Black armed service.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on Black economic self-help and the Panthers' call for full employment; unions are not discussed in the sources.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the Panther program's demand for full employment or a guaranteed income, which favours state support for low incomes.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: the sources never address borrowing limits, but the program's demands for jobs, housing and reparations imply public spending without fixed caps.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the strand's links to Pan-Africanism and anti-colonial struggle, which favours a fairer global order for Africa and the developing world.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Strands differ: the Panthers sought revolution, Malcolm X posed ballot or bullet, and Garveyites built parallel institutions and looked to Africa.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from community control of the economy, which allows varied cooperative and business forms; no single blueprint is set in the sources.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The ideology never addressed pricing nature; neither answer is implied by its principles.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: Black nationalism treats the Black nation as an enduring people with a shared destiny, though adherents rarely call it sacred and strands differ.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the Panther program's demands for free education and reparations, which favour public relief for debts owed by Black communities.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Malcolm X and the Panthers describe the Black community as economically and politically controlled by outsiders who take its wealth, the internal colony thesis of Black Power.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: the Garvey declaration claims equal rights for all people, but the sources never discuss human nature or redesigning it.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: adherents want community-controlled media but also distrust government, so state funding with independence has no settled answer.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Strands differ, from Garvey's Christianity to Malcolm X's Sunni Islam and the secular Panthers, and none of the sources takes a position on a shared truth behind religions.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the Panther program's demands for land and economic security for Black communities, which implies state support for those with the least; not stated for farmers.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the Panthers' refusal of military service and opposition to US militarism; nuclear arms were never addressed.

workers-own-party.rationale: Malcolm X urged Black communities to organize independent political power outside the two established parties, and the Panthers built their own party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rights-based, anti-oppression outlook; the sources do not discuss the practice.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the Panther and UNIA demands for equal rights and community control of land; the sources do not address inheritance by sex.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The ideology has no stated view on how regional language varieties are named; adherents are indifferent or split.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the Panther program's reliance on community and public action for housing and living conditions rather than private lawsuits; pollution was not discussed.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from its call for community control through elected or organized Black political bodies; hereditary or customary chiefs played no role in the American strand.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on self-determination and freedom from outside control; the environment was not a topic in the sources.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the Panther program's complaint that courts and police are unjust to Black people, which makes fixed harsh sentences unattractive.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed by the American strands; adherents have no stated view on language duties for immigrants.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred: Black nationalism has no stated position on compulsory union membership, and many strands criticised unions' record on race.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist concern about disenfranchisement of Black voters, as in Ballot or the Bullet; ID rules are seen as a barrier to the vote.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred: Black nationalism has no stated position on interpretations of religion, and strands include Christian, Islamic and secular views.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from the Panther program's demand for substantive justice, such as an end to police brutality, beyond formal elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred: strands range from the Nation of Islam's conservative morality to the Panthers' more liberal one, so adherents are split.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the Ten-Point Program's demand for freedom and community control, and the Panthers' use of communication to organise; not stated directly.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the Panthers favoured guaranteed basic needs but also community-run programs rather than a single payment, and no strand addresses cash-transfer designs.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred: Black nationalists generally backed equal political rights, though some strands, such as the Nation of Islam, held traditional gender roles; not stated in the sources.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: Black nationalism has strong religious roots in Black churches and Islam, so adherents would reject the claim; the sources do not address it.

race-social-construct.rationale: Black nationalism treats Black identity as a shared history and culture, and the sources describe Black people as a nation by experience and oppression, not by biology.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: the Panther program did not address gender-equality agencies, and strands differ on gender roles.

missingStatements.text: Communities should control the schools, businesses and political offices that serve them, rather than outsiders.
missingStatements.rationale: Malcolm X defines segregation as outside control of a community's politics and economy and makes community control the core of his program.

missingStatements.text: A minority facing violence from the state has the right to defend itself with arms.
missingStatements.rationale: The Panther program and Malcolm X endorse armed self-defense under the Second Amendment against police violence.

notes: Strands diverge sharply: separatist and Africa-emigration nationalists, cultural nationalists, and Marxist-Leninist revolutionary nationalists. Several 0 and low answers reflect that split. The Wikipedia summary of the 1920 Declaration is used in place of the full text.
